title: A CDC milestone is what at least three quarters of children do by an age
summary: On the CDC milestone pages, a milestone is something most children, 75 percent or more, can do by a given age.
body: The CDC 15-month page says developmental milestones are things most children, 75 percent or more, can do by a certain age. That is a group description. It is not a statement that every child does the thing. The same pages tell caregivers that missing a milestone is a reason to talk with the doctor and ask about developmental screening. The figure is the United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention list. Lists published in other countries can pick different ages.

sources.title: Milestones by 15 Months
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US federal page, public domain. Opened 2026-11-26. Reviewed date on the page is 16 May 2026. Supports the sentence that milestones are things most children (75% or more) can do by a certain age, and the instruction to talk with the doctor and ask about screening.
